facts.text: Nikolai takes its name from Chief Nikolai, a late‑19th‑century leader who settled the area and guided its early community.
In the 1830s, Peter Kolmakov opened a temporary trading post near present‑day Aniak, trading tobacco and cloth for beaver pelts.
Nikolai officially incorporated as a city on July 9, 1970, marking its formal municipal status.
The current site of Nikolai was established around 1918 near a historic trading post and roadhouse on the Rainy Pass Trail during the gold rush era.
Nicholas Orthodox Church, built in Nikolai, serves as a central community and cultural landmark for residents.
The Upper Kuskokwim Athabascan people, known as Dichinanek’ Hwt’ana, inhabited the Nikolai region with a semi‑nomadic hunter‑gatherer lifestyle adapted to the boreal forest and riverine environment.
